title: Cooling coffee: two models compared with residuals

stimulus.title: Temperature of a cup of coffee
stimulus.text: A cup of coffee is left on a table in a room kept at $22$ degrees Celsius. Its temperature is measured every $5$ minutes. Two models are proposed: a linear model $L$, found by linear regression on the data, and the model $E$ given by $E(t) = 22 + 70(0.952)^t$, where $t$ is in minutes and both models give degrees Celsius.

table.caption: Temperature of the coffee, in degrees Celsius, t minutes after it is poured

parts.label: A(i)
parts.prompt: Use linear regression on the data to find $L(t) = mt + c$. Give $m$ and $c$ as decimal approximations.

rubric.point: $m = -2.168$ and $c = 89.120$ (correct to three decimal places; both needed)
accept: values truncated to three decimal places

parts.sample: Linear regression on the lists gives $m = -2.168000$ and $c = 89.120000$, so $L(t) = -2.168000t + 89.120000$. Both values are stored.

parts.label: A(ii)
parts.prompt: A residual is the actual value minus the predicted value. Find the residual of $L$ and the residual of $E$ at $t = 10$.

rubric.point: Residual of $L$: $-2.440$; residual of $E$: $0.198$ (both, as actual minus predicted)
accept: values truncated to three decimal places

parts.label: B(i)
parts.prompt: The residuals of $L$ at $t = 0, 5, 10, 15, 20$ are, in order, positive, negative, negative, negative, positive. The residuals of $E$ are all within $0.5$ of $0$ with no pattern. Which model is more appropriate for the data? Give a reason for your answer.

rubric.point: $E$, with a reason from the residuals: the residuals of $E$ are small with no pattern, while those of $L$ show a pattern (positive, negative, positive)
accept: "E: its residuals are close to 0 and patternless; L's residuals form a U, so the data curve away from the line"

parts.sample: $E$ is more appropriate. Its residuals are small and show no pattern. The residuals of $L$ go from positive to negative and back to positive, so the data bend upward away from the line, and a line has the wrong shape.

parts.label: B(ii)
parts.prompt: Use the model $E$ to predict the temperature of the coffee at $t = 30$ minutes.

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: (i) Use $E$ to find the time when the coffee is $40$ degrees Celsius. (ii) Explain why the model $L$ should not be used to predict the temperature an hour after the coffee is poured.

rubric.point: (i) $t = 27.610$ minutes, from solving $E(t) = 40$ with a calculator
accept: an intersection of y = E(t) and y = 40 reported to three decimal places

rubric.point: (ii) $L$ is decreasing without bound: it falls below the room temperature of $22$ degrees after about $t = 31.0$ minutes, which a cooling cup in a $22$-degree room cannot do
accept: a reason tied to the room temperature and the line decreasing forever

parts.sample: (i) Graph $y = E(t)$ and $y = 40$ and find the intersection: $t = 27.610$ minutes. (ii) $L$ has a negative slope, so it keeps decreasing at the same rate. $L(60) = -40.960$ degrees, below the room temperature of $22$ degrees; in fact $L(t) < 22$ for $t > 30.959$. Coffee in a $22$-degree room cools toward $22$ degrees and does not drop below it, so $L$ is not valid an hour after pouring. $E$ approaches $22$, since $\lim_{t \to \infty} E(t) = 22$.
